query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In solidified, cast Co‐free FeNiCrMn, the dynamic mechanical response across variable strain rates and temperatures is governed by the strain rate– and temperature–dependent activation of localized adiabatic shear bands that enhance dislocation mobility and work hardening, thereby maintaining the strength–ductility balance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, solidified single-phase (or near-single-phase) Co‐free FeNiCrMn alloy with a homogeneous microstructure.
generation.intervention: Subject specimens to controlled dynamic deformation tests (tension or compression) while varying strain rates (from quasi-static to high rates) and temperatures (e.g., cryogenic, room temperature, and elevated temperatures).
generation.conditions: Tests performed under identical processing history (as-cast state without post-annealing) across a matrix of strain rates and temperatures to isolate dynamic effects. Use continuous strain monitoring and high-speed imaging for deformation mapping.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of adiabatic shear bands that locally refine the microstructure and concentrate dislocation processes.
generation.mechanism: At high strain rates and/or elevated temperatures, deformation localizes into transient adiabatic shear bands. The rapid local adiabatic heating within these bands enhances dislocation mobility and triggers additional dislocation multiplication while preserving overall ductility. In contrast, at low strain rates the deformation is more uniform with lower local temperature rises, leading to a different balance between strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Under high strain rate and elevated temperature conditions, the dynamic yield strength increases due to enhanced strain hardening from localized shear band formation, without a severe loss in ductility. Conversely, at lower strain rates or lower temperatures, deformation is more homogeneous with relatively lower dynamic yield strength.
generation.baseline: Quasi-static, room temperature tests where homogeneous deformation is observed with standard work-hardening behavior and no pronounced shear band formation.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies specifically to as-cast, homogeneous Co‐free FeNiCrMn alloys; it may not extend to alloys with significant post-casting microstructural modifications (e.g., recrystallized or heavily precipitated states) or compositions that depart from the Co-free constraint.
generation.uncertainty: The exact thresholds (in strain rate and temperature) at which the transition from uniform deformation to localized shear banding occurs remain uncertain and may be affected by subtle variations in grain size, residual defects, or minor compositional inhomogeneities.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of identical as-cast Co‐free FeNiCrMn specimens and subject them to deformation tests in both tension and compression. Use a controlled testing rig capable of varying strain rate (spanning quasi-static to high dynamic rates) and temperature (from cryogenic to elevated conditions). Equip specimens with high-speed imaging and in situ temperature sensors, and perform post-mortem electron microscopy (e.g., SEM/TEM) to map local microstructural evolution.
measurements: Dynamic yield strength and work hardening rate as a function of strain rate and temperature.
Local temperature rise measurements during deformation.
Identification and quantification of adiabatic shear bands (e.g., their density, width, and distribution) via high-speed imaging and post-mortem microstructural analysis.
Dislocation density in shear band regions vs. non-shear band regions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If, under high strain rate and/or elevated temperature conditions, no localized regions of adiabatic heating (i.e., shear bands) are observed or if the dynamic yield strength and work hardening behavior do not significantly differ from quasi-static conditions, then the hypothesis that dynamic performance is mediated by adiabatic shear band formation and associated dislocation effects would be falsified.

High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are new alloys that contain five or more elements in roughly-equal proportion. We present new experiments and theory on the deformation behavior of HEAs under slow stretching (straining), and observe differences, compared to conventional alloys with fewer elements. For a specific range of temperatures and strain-rates, HEAs deform in a jerky way, with sudden slips that make it difficult to precisely control the deformation. An analytic model explains these slips as avalanches of slipping weak spots and predicts the observed slip statistics, stress-strain curves, and their dependence on temperature, strain-rate, and material composition. The ratio of the weak spots’ healing rate to the strain-rate is the main tuning parameter, reminiscent of the Portevin-LeChatellier effect and time-temperature superposition in polymers. Our model predictions agree with the experimental results. The proposed widely-applicable deformation mechanism is useful for deformation control and alloy design.
